note: ungraded per-product layers (RGBA, straight alpha) and shadows (grey RGB, multiply) in work-r6/; grade_cut_r6.py grades and cuts them with the ONE v3c grade; the numbers here are measured on graded scenes recomposed with the change (set B)

vase.what: re-cut from the raw render (QA R5 3.1: the cut followed R4's placeholder and lost the lit flank); straightened and sized to the card about the foot; colour

method.edges: the vase's silhouette as the model drew it, row by row on its body (the rim + 3 to the foot's contact): the edges are the     sub-pixel peaks of the render's own colour gradient (Lab, sigma-0.6 blur; central differences): the right edge within 8 px inside /     3 px outside the old cut's (QA found that side right); the left edge within a window round the right edge's mirror about the     axis. The axis is fitted as a line on the rows where both edges are found (robust: two rounds, residuals over 2 px dropped), the     windows narrowed round it (10 px, then 5 px). The half width r(y) = (right - left) / 2, outliers against a 7-row median (> 1.5 px)     replaced by it, then smoothed (sigma 1.5 rows): a turned body is smooth. Returns per body row the axis and r, and the record
method.alpha: the re-cut alpha in the render's own coordinates: the body rows from the profile (the old cut's soft bottom row kept as a vertical     falloff), the old cut above the body (the lip, the branch)
method.straighten_and_size: the forward affine (render -> layer): the axis made vertical about the foot (x - tilt (y - foot_y): the camera is level, the     window's mullion is vertical in the same render, so the model's lean is the model's), then the card's size about the foot (sx, sy);     applied premultiplied (bilinear). Returns rgb, alpha, the matrix, the foot's axis x
method.shadow: extract.shadow_one (frozen, pass_r5.shadow_new) on the final cut, against the scene behind, on the render carried by the layer's own affine

axis_check_in_layer.how: the alpha 0.5 mid-points of the body rows

colour.fix: the default vase: R5's a*b* fix re-solved on the re-cut body (post_r5.vase_colour's method and targets: one hue rotation and one     chroma factor for every body pixel, rows >= 935; the hue of the surfaces beside, L* unchanged), started from R5's dh and k. With its lit     flank back the lit half is lighter (L* 88 against R5's 79) and R5's k alone gives C* 3.4, under the designer's 4-7 and cooler than     the room's own white (the back wall, C* 4.05): the lit half is set to C* 4.5, inside the range and the nearest to the card's     near-neutral #EEECE8

curtains-v2.what: 554205 (curtains-aliexpress-beige-linen-sheer-curtains-554205, hooks 150 x 270, SKU 12000029601125492), now variant 2: L* and a*b* relative to 180502 (designer section 1)
curtains-v2.method: 554205 as variant 2 (designer section 1, 'the fix of 554205'): relative to 180502 in the same light and under the same mask (QA     p2_colour's mask on each layer, intersected), L* included. (1) The lightness: ONE monotone tone curve on the low frequencies of L*     (a normalised blur over the curtain, sigma 1.5 fold spacings = 75 px, i.e. a kernel about 3 spacings wide): the low-frequency L*     quantiles of 554205 mapped onto 180502's (the same mask, the ungraded layers), shifted so the graded medians meet; the high     frequencies (the folds, sigma 3-75, and the slub, under sigma 3) back x g, g = (L*180502 + 16) / (L*554205 + 16) clipped to 1-1.2     (a brighter cloth shows the same folds as larger L* steps); two soft shoulders (the folds' crests over 89, the slub's specks over     93.5) keep the brightest folds under burn (target 5). (2) The colour after the lightness: a*b* by R5's method (one hue rotation, one chroma     factor for every pixel) to 180502's median C* and h. (3) The armchair post's line solved again (fix_r5.post_line_fix). The free alpha     and the shadow layer are 554205's own, unchanged

masks.same_mask: QA p2_colour's mask (alpha 255 eroded 5 x 5, rows 100-1400) of 554205 AND of 180502: 305301 px
masks.clean_ring: 15-40 px out of both curtains, no product (both curtains, every slot and variant, the cushion sets), no furniture, L* > 80 (plaster, not glass): 22846 px (QA R5: the targets' old ring was 23 % curtain)

tone_curve.bands: low = the normalised blur (sigma 75); folds = blur 3 - low; slub = L - blur 3
tone_curve.formula: L* = top(shoulder(curve(low) + offset + g folds) + g slub); shoulder: above 89, 89 + 3 tanh((L - 89) / 3); top: above 93.5, 93.5 + 2 tanh((L - 93.5) / 2) (the crests and the slub's specks under burn, target 5)

framed-art-v2.what: the seam anti-aliased along every rail, the default's inner shadow line kept; the light specks out; R5's black lift
framed-art-v2.method: framed-art v2 (QA R5 3.5; the designer section 5): the seam between the default's walnut band and the variant's prints, along all     six rails, anti-aliased. Each print area's four sides are ONE sub-pixel line each (fitted through R5's integer staircase, which     followed the moulding's measured offset from the frame's outer edge); per pixel the coverage (8 x 8 samples) of three zones: the print     (inside the lines), the default's inner line (the 1.2 px just outside them: the dark shadow line the default's top mouldings end     with; its colour from the default's own whole pixels there, sigma 1.5 along the rail) and the moulding (beyond: the default's own     pixels, unchanged wherever a pixel is fully moulding). Each line is fitted on the default's own moulding -> print edge where the     default's print beside it is light (_default_edge_lines), else through R5's staircase. The print's colour next to the line is carried from 2.5 px inside (a normalised blur,     sigma 1.5: the render's light-oak frame was wider than the walnut band, as R5). R5's black lift on the prints, the same lift. Then the     isolated light specks in the prints' black (QA: L* > the neighbours' + 25 with 7 of 8 neighbours black) take their neighbours' median
